## Where do the docs say to look first for SilverBullet logs, and how much history does that place keep?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Revisions.md] ---
### Browsing history

# Browsing history
If revisions are enabled, there will be two additional views in the editor:

* ${widgets.commandButton("Revision: Page History")} lists the current page’s revisions, newest first. Selecting one opens a preview showing the change as a colour-coded diff, switch to **Content** to read the whole page as it was at that point. **Restore** puts that version back into the editor as a single undo step.
* ${widgets.commandButton("Revision: Space History")} lists commits across the whole space.

Whatever has changed since the last commit heads both views as an **Uncommitted changes** entry — in the space-wide log it opens up to list every file involved. Selecting it shows the change. There is nothing to restore, since it is what is already on disk.

### Find your way

# Find your way
* [[Getting Started|Start here]] — learn [[Markdown]], connect [[Page|Pages]], add [[Tag|Tags]] and [[Meta Page]] and try queries in [[Workbench]]. Each guide stands on its own.
* [[Guides]] — practical tasks and use cases for personal knowledge, team collaboration and docs as code.
* [[Administration|Setup and administration]] — install and operate Desktop or Server, and back up your space.
* [[Reference]] — look up feature behavior, syntax and APIs.
* [[Development|Contributing]] — help develop SilverBullet, its documentation and extensions.

As you will have figured, these docs run inside a read-only instance of SilverBullet. It in itself aims to be a good-practice use of [Docs as Code](https://silverbullet.md/docs-as-code). [[Guide/Reading These Docs]] explains how to inspect examples and try them in your own writable space.
